title: Elastic bucket (gamma) proto - personal backfill
content:
Quick brain-dump of an alternate credit model: elastic buckets with a decay/gamma curve. Meant as a tiny prototype to reason about activation, burst, and long-tail usage without pure timebound credits.

Motivation
- Credits/buckets are messy: either you give flat session credits (wasteful) or pure per-token (psychologically painful). Want something that: a) gives new users a visible "burst budget" for activation, b) gracefully decays allowance for low-value background usage, c) rewards stickiness by letting high-quality sessions use more of the bucket over time.

High-level design
- Each account gets a monthly "elastic bucket" size B (in token-equivalent units).
- Consumption is charged against B first with an internal cost multiplier m(t) that depends on recency and session intensity.
- Unused portion of B decays by factor gamma per day: leftover_{t+1} = leftover_t * (1 - gamma). Gamma in [0,0.1] typically.
- When B is exhausted, fallback to pay-as-you-go (PAYG) at public rate, or soft-throttle depending on tier.
- Buckets top up monthly and have optional auto-roll (small carryover) with penalty to discourage hoarding.

Key knobs (B, gamma, m(session)) and intuition:
- B controls breadth of activation (onboarding size). Higher B => larger activation but higher cost.
- Gamma controls retention of buffer for long-tail. Low gamma => long carry -> favors seasonal users. High gamma -> encourages frequent engagement.
- m(session) can implement session weighting: e.g., interactive UI sessions get m=0.8 (discounted against bucket), background batch jobs get m=1.2 (penalized). This nudges product alignment.

B/OE math (back-of-envelope)
Assumptions (baseline model):
- Model baseline inference cost to Redwood (amortized infra + GPU ops + misc) ~ $0.000012 per token (i.e., $0.012 per 1k tokens).
- Target gross margin target at hosted plan layer: 75% -> target customer price per 1k tokens = $0.048. (Because we charge customers higher than infra cost).
- Average session length: 600 tokens (prompt + reply).
- Activation conversion target: give activation bucket that supports ~12 high-quality sessions for first-week trial -> B_target_tokens = 12 * 600 = 7,200 tokens.

If B = 7,200 tokens, internal cost = 7,200 * $0.000012 = $0.0864 (infra cost). If we allocate a nominal list price "value" for the bucket at 12 sessions priced at avg $0.048/1k -> 7.2k tokens * ($0.048/1000) = $0.3456 perceived value. So unit subsidy = $0.3456 - $0.0864 = $0.2592 (we're subsidizing activation).

Gamma tuning example:
- If gamma = 0.03/day (3% decay), leftover after 30 days = (1-0.03)^30 ≈ 0.40. So 60% of unspent bucket evaporates — good to limit long-term hoarding.
- If gamma = 0.005/day (0.5%), leftover ≈ 0.86 -> gentle decay, useful for SMB where we want to be sticky.

Session multiplier m examples (behavioral incentives):
- Interactive prompt chat (human-facing) m = 0.8 (bucket charges 0.8 * tokens) -> effectively extends bucket by 25% for interactive usage.
- Embedding generation heavy batch m = 1.3 -> eats bucket faster (we want customers to move heavy embed workloads to dedicated reserved pools).
- Memory/long-context calls (large seq length) m = 1.5 for sequences > 8k tokens.

Margin and utilization heuristics
Goal: keep expected subsidy per new activated user below $1 for GA.
- Suppose conversion probability from trial to paid = p_conv = 6% (conservative). Expected subsidy per converted user = subsidy_given / p_conv. So to keep subsidy_per_converted < $5, subsidy_given < $0.30. With above activation subsidy ~ $0.26 -> borderline but okay.
- Sensitivity: if p_conv drops to 3%, subsidy_per_converted = $0.26 / 0.03 ≈ $8.66 -> too high. So B/gamma need to be tuned to maintain econ.

Example tier sketches (rough):
- Nano (free/onramp): B = 5k tokens, gamma=0.04/day, m_interactive=0.9, carryover cap 10%
- Starter (free+paid starter): B = 20k tokens, gamma=0.02/day, m_interactive=0.8, carryover 25%
- Pro (paid monthly): B = 200k tokens, gamma=0.005/day, m_interactive=0.75, includes 5 concurrent session slots, ability to pin model variants
- Dedicated / Reserved: no bucket (or infinite internal bucket but behind commit), heavy embedding discounts (m_embed=0.6)

Questions / unknowns / TODO
- How to represent bucket value in billing UI so it "feels" like free but not misleading? (show token balance and equivalent $ value?)
- Edge cases: long-running background jobs that intentionally split into many short calls to exploit m values. Need server-side detection and reweighting.
- Rate-limiting interactions with bucket: if customer uses 3x concurrency, does decay behave differently? Probably tie gamma to actual calendar days regardless of concurrency.
- Integrations with Dedicated: map bucket discounts to reserved capacity credits for teams on reserved contracts.
- Tracking: need telemetry to track bucket usage, per-session multiplier attribution, and conversion lift (A/B test bucket sizes & gamma).

Small A/B test plan (quick):
- Cohort A: B=7.2k, gamma=0.03
- Cohort B: B=3.5k, gamma=0.03
- Compare activation -> D7 retention -> conv at 14/30 days. Metric: conversion per dollar subsidy and engagement lift.

Possible visual/UX ideas (notes to self)
- Show "Burst balance" in product header: remaining tokens + estimated sessions left (using interactive-weighted average).
- Add a CTA: "Buy extra burst" at micro-prices when bucket dips below 20%. Micro-buys at discounted PAYG price.
- Email nudge if bucket unused for 7 days and >50% left: "Try these starter flows" to increase utilization (drives product engagement).

Closing loose thoughts
- This model sits between pure credits and subscription: gives psychologically neat burst, prevents hoarding, and nudges product-to-dedicated migration.
- Biggest risk is complexity in explaining multipliers and decay; keep default simple (show only balance and sessions estimate) and expose knobs in billing docs for power users.

Quick TODOs:
- Run a tiny cost sim (Monte Carlo) with 10k synthetic users to see expected subsidy distribution (Jon can help with simple script).
- Draft short FAQ for UX explaining gamma and m.
- Wireframe bucket display in console (Sophie to sketch).

Notes to self: keep this doc small and messy — convert to formal PRD only if A/B looks promising.

End of dump.
